title: Which quadratic families have maximal prime runs, and what discriminants do they correspond to?
statement: n^2+n+q has a full prime run for n=0..q-2 exactly when q in {2,3,5,11,17,41}, corresponding to Heegner discriminants -7,-11,-19,-43,-67,-163 (Rabinowitsch 1913). Generalize: for other quadratic families an^2+bn+c, characterize maximal prime runs and their discriminant correspondence.
why: Directly extends the result the arena already derived. Classical theory exists for the principal form; the computational question of which families give long runs and whether the correspondence is as clean is concrete and checkable.
forges: tabulate the RIGHT invariant; a bound derived in one regime does not survive optimisation in another

title: Is the list of 65 idoneal numbers complete?
statement: Euler's idoneal numbers: n such that x^2+ny^2 represents a number in essentially one way only when that number is prime, a prime power, or twice one. 65 are known, largest 1848. Conjectured complete; at most one more can exist, and none under GRH.
why: Genuinely open, same circle of ideas as the Heegner correspondence, and computationally explorable. Any structural constraint found on a hypothetical 66th is real.
forges: derive constraints on a hypothetical object nobody has found

title: Does phi(n) | n-1 force n prime?
statement: Lehmer's totient problem: if phi(n) divides n-1, must n be prime? No composite example is known. Known constraints: a counterexample must be odd, squarefree, and have at least 15 prime factors.
why: Constraint-tightening is tractable in hours even though the search space is astronomically out of reach. The value is retiring structure, not finding n.
forges: recognise a wall early; park with the reason so the approach is not re-derived

title: Is Giuga's congruence prime-exclusive?
statement: Giuga: n is prime iff sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) = -1 mod n. The forward direction is Fermat; the converse is open. A counterexample must be a Carmichael-like number satisfying strong joint conditions.
why: The counterexample conditions are checkable and compose with Carmichael structure. Good target for constraint derivation.
forges: REDUCE a conjecture to a sharper sub-question; attack an intersection rather than filtering one set by the other

title: Are 4, 5, 7 the only n with n!+1 a perfect square?
statement: Brocard's problem: n!+1 = m^2 has known solutions n=4,5,7 (m=5,11,71). Searched past 10^9 with none further.
why: Modular obstructions are cheap to compute and the search-space retirement is honest even though a full search is hopeless.
forges: cheap modular obstructions as search-space retirement

title: Is the multiplicity of an integer in Pascal's triangle bounded?
statement: Singmaster's conjecture: there is an absolute bound on how many times an integer >1 appears in Pascal's triangle. 3003 appears 8 times; no number is known to appear more.
why: Multiplicity-8 numbers come from simultaneous binomial identities tied to Fibonacci-like recurrences. Concrete search with real structure to find.
forges: find simultaneous structure across two identities

title: FORGE: generate and break conjectures about polynomial prime-run records
statement: Search wide families of integer polynomials for prime-run records, form the sharpest conjecture the data supports, then attack that conjecture rather than defending it.
why: Nobody has looked at most of this space. A forged conjecture that breaks in ten minutes cost ten minutes; one that survives is a small real result.
forges: form the sharpest conjecture the data supports, then attack rather than defend it

title: FORGE: fixed points and cycles of digit-power maps in mixed bases
statement: Maps like n -> sum of d-th powers of base-b digits have known cycles for b=10. Explore other bases and exponents, conjecture cycle-structure laws from the data, then try to falsify them.
why: Cheap to compute exhaustively below the natural bound, so conjectures can be settled rather than merely supported.
forges: reduce to a DECIDABLE family so results are theorems; group by a derived invariant, not the raw parameter

title: FORGE: structure in aliquot sequence behaviour
statement: Aliquot sequences (iterate sum of proper divisors) either terminate, cycle, or are open. Look for statistical or structural regularities, conjecture, and attack.
why: Large open catalogue, and driver-based heuristics give real structure to conjecture about.
forges: conjecture from statistics over a large open catalogue

title: FORGE: primality density in low-order integer recurrences
statement: For families like a(n+1)=k*a(n)+m, look for parameter choices with anomalous prime density, conjecture a law, then break it.
why: Enormous unexplored parameter space with cheap evaluation.
forges: search an enormous cheap parameter space for anomaly, then distinguish signal from selection effect

title: Kaprekar routines in arbitrary base and digit-length
statement: The map n -> (digits descending) - (digits ascending). Base 10 with 4 digits converges to the constant 6174; with 3 digits to 495. For general (base b, length L) the structure of fixed points and cycles is far less catalogued.
why: FULLY DECIDABLE per (b,L) - the map is closed on L-digit strings, so exhaustive enumeration SETTLES each case. Same shape as the digit-power win, and lib/digitmaps.py technique transfers. Theorems, not searches.
forges: exploit state-space collapse (multiset, not integer); sanity-check against a known value BEFORE trusting a method

title: Is multiplicative persistence bounded, and what happens in other bases?
statement: Multiplicative persistence: iterate n -> product of digits until a single digit. Base 10 record is 11, at 277777788888899, and it is CONJECTURED no number exceeds 11 (open). The base-b analogue is far less studied.
why: GENUINELY OPEN and searchable. Base 10 has been pushed to ~10^233 by others, but most other bases are barely explored - a record or an unbounded-looking base would be a real find rather than a rediscovery.
forges: check the argmax against the search ceiling; reduce a search to the IMAGE of the map

title: Palindrome-reversal dynamics across bases
statement: Iterate n -> n + reverse(n). In base 10 whether 196 ever reaches a palindrome is open. In base 2 it is PROVED that 10110 never does. Which bases admit proved Lychrel numbers, and is there a structural criterion?
why: Base 2 has a proof, base 10 does not - the gap between them is the interesting part, and intermediate bases are under-explored. A proved Lychrel in a new base is a real result.
forges: compile multi-interface words to exact polynomials in b^n; next symbolically lift the verified base-17 topology across the base parameter and solve coefficient plus digit-range constraints

title: FORGE: conjectures stated on thin evidence
statement: Many integer-sequence conjectures are asserted from a handful of terms. Systematically generate such claims from short data, then extend the computation far past the stated evidence and look for the break.
why: This is where conjectures ACTUALLY break. A claim supported by 20 terms and never rechecked is the highest-yield target class available.
forges: extend far past the evidence a claim was built on — the core falsification skill

title: Is 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z solvable for every n >= 2?
statement: Erdos-Straus conjecture. Verified past 10^17. Solvability is governed by congruence classes of n; only n in certain residue classes mod 840 are hard.
why: Highly structured: the hard residues are a finite explicit set, so identifying which classes resist an identity is concrete constraint work rather than blind search.
forges: work a finite explicit residue structure instead of blind search

title: FORGE: digit-product and mixed digit maps
statement: Beyond sums of powers: products of digits, alternating sums, digit maps weighted by position. Each family is decidable below a bound, so laws can be SETTLED. Test whether T5's congruence-boost law (T(n)=n mod gcd(b-1,M_d)) has an analogue.
why: Directly extends the arena's one proved law into an adjacent family. If the congruence mechanism generalises it is a real structural result; if it fails the failure is informative.
forges: test whether a proved mechanism GENERALISES to an adjacent family
